feature: A ring or arc arrives spinning
summary: In an icon frame, adding Rotation to a ring or an arc now arrives as a spinner: 0 to 360, Linear, Forever, one turn every 1.2 seconds. Every other shape still arrives as the small swing.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Make a 24 unit icon frame (New Frame, Icons, 24) and zoom to 800%.
Draw an arc with the pen: click, drag a bend, click, press Return.
In Motion, press the plus and choose Rotation.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw a ring with the ellipse tool, select it and add Rotation the same way.
Draw a box, select it and add Rotation: it swings back and forth as before.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does the arc start spinning the moment you add Rotation, with nothing to retype?
Is 1.2 seconds a turn the right pace to start from for a spinner?
Is it right that an ellipse on an ordinary picture (not in an icon frame) still arrives as the swing?
rough: The arc turns about its own middle when it arrives, as the mock's step 3 draws it, so it orbits until Around is set to Artboard (step 4). That matches the mock.
A closed curve drawn whole (a ball, a bell) still swings; only a ring, an open bent line, or a curve with part of its line trimmed away counts as a spinner.
A ring on a layer that sits on a video's timeline keeps the swing that plays once, since a video finishes rather than repeats.
